title: Statistical Inference in Causal Partial Identification under Smooth Densities
claim: Our estimator's error decays with sample size at least as fast as existing baselines, and faster in some settings.
layout: 3 panels side-by-side, shared legend style, error bars on line plots
description: Three side-by-side line plots comparing estimation error against sample size n, running from about 750 to 2500. Panels are labeled (a) Location model, (b) Quadratic model and (c) Scale model. Each panel has three curves with error bars: Wavelet-CW in blue with circles, LL-kNN in orange with squares, and Plugin in green with triangles. The legend sits inside each plot. In (a), LL-kNN stays high and flat at about 0.0015, while Wavelet-CW and Plugin are much lower and noisy. In (b), all curves decline, and Wavelet-CW drops fastest, from about 0.0005 to 0.0003. In (c), LL-kNN stays near 0.0005, while Wavelet-CW and Plugin sit close together near 0.0001. The eye goes first to the orange curve, which is clearly separated, and to the blue curve, which ends lowest.
caption: Plots of estimation error comparison of our method (Wavelet CW estimate) with \parencite{ji2023model} (LL-kNN, for which we use `knn"-based nuisance estimator) and \parencite{lin2025estimation} (Plugin) with $d_Y=1$, $d_Z=1$. The estimation error is defined by $\EE[|V_{\cc} - \widehat V_{\cc}|]$. The mean error curve and the corresponding standard-error confidence bands are computed by aggregating results over 100 Monte Carlo repetitions. The plots show that the convergence rate of our method is at least comparable with the existing approaches in low dimension.
abstract: Many causal quantities are only partially identifiable due to the inherent missingness of potential outcomes, and the associated partial identification (PI) sets can be obtained by solving an optimal transport (OT) problem. Covariates often provide additional information about the potential outcomes and thus yield tighter PI sets, which can be obtained via conditional optimal transport (COT). However, COT-based PI set estimators are susceptible to the curse of dimensionality in the covariates and outcomes, which precludes the asymptotic normality and hinders statistical inference. In this paper, we exploit smoothness in the marginal densities of covariates and potential outcomes and develop a wavelet-based primal method for COT with multivariate outcomes and covariates. Moreover, for quadratic cost functions, we establish a stability result for COT and prove asymptotic normality of the proposed estimator. This characterization of the asymptotic distribution enables valid statistical inference for the partial identification set. Empirically, we validate the estimation and inference performance of our approach through numerical experiments in comparison with existing benchmarks.
